mission: Help a Florida Panhandle or coastal Alabama reader make a better property decision with verifiable reporting, clear math and practical judgment.

pillars.name: Financing and the economy
decisions: what a data release changes locally

pillars.name: Local market conditions
decisions: read inventory by property type and area

pillars.name: Selling and equity
decisions: sell or keep as a rental

pillars.name: Mid-term rentals and ownership operations
primarySources: actual redacted leases and operating records

selectionOrder: dated observed search or recurring-client demand
runnable editorial queue with coverage gaps as tie-breakers
sourceRules: Open the primary source this session. A search snippet or model summary is discovery, not verification.
Keep publication date, effective date, collection date, measurement window, geography and property type distinct.
Label reported facts, calculations, hypothetical scenarios, forecasts and judgment separately.
Document five load-bearing checks. Use fewer market statistics and more transparent hypothetical math if primary data is unavailable.
A law, proposal, adopted rule and effective rule are different states. An address and jurisdiction are required for rental eligibility claims.
Gross rental revenue is not profit. State occupancy denominator, owner-use nights, management, utilities, maintenance, insurance, taxes, debt service and reserves.
MTR or a longer stay is not an automatic exemption from licensing, taxes, zoning or association restrictions. Verify each applicable rule.
Use explicit downside assumptions; never promise appreciation, occupancy, rental income or a future refinancing opportunity.

voice.style: A capable local real estate adviser explaining one decision to one reader. Specific, calm and candid.
editPass: Does the opening answer the actual question?
Can a reader use the example?
Does every local reference change the decision?
Remove repetitive summaries, clichés and stock transitions.
Read it aloud. Vary sentence length and remove anything a person would not say.

seoGeo.principle: Crawlable, useful HTML, accurate entities and schema, distinctive reporting, contextual links and clear answers. No ranking promises.
seoGeo.faq: Useful visible questions and matching schema. Do not promise Google FAQ rich results for this business.
seoGeo.schema: BlogPosting, canonical author/publisher references and BreadcrumbList. Never add fabricated reviews, credentials or unsupported property data.
seoGeo.titles: Describe the decision honestly. Include a number only if it helps, is supported and will stay correct until review.
